messages.author: 4ddc99c6029ba75d
messages.subject: Shapefile question
parts:
Hi:
I was wondering if somebody could look at the two pictures attached to
the link
below and give advice on why ggplot is not
filling the color in one of the shapes (wasatch and Uinta Mountains).
If I use
spplot it fills out the color correctly but can't figure out why
ggplot is only
coloring two regions of wasatch and Uinta Mountains and leaving
one(pointing
with arrow) unfilled. The link to the shapefile and pictures:

# Save the shapefile to your working directory and run the code below:
https://secure.filesanywhere.com/fs/v.aspx?v=8a69658a586174b873a6

# Load the packages needed
library(spsurvey)
library(maptools)
gpclibPermit()

# Read in the shapefile
shp <- read.shape("eco_l3_ut")
dim(shp)
# Convert the "shp" shapefile to dataframe to design the GRTS
(Equalsites)
shp_attributes <- as.data.frame(shp);shp_attributes
# Summarise frame by ecoregion
ddply(shp_attributes,"level3_nam",summarise,Total=round(sum(area_ha),
0))
# Convert "shp" to dataframe again but this time to be used wit
ggplot2 and then
# inspect the shapefile to see what variable can be used for region
when we
# apply the "fortify.SpatialPolygonsDataFrame" function to it.
shp.DF <- as.data.frame(shp)
head(shp.DF)
names(shp)

# fortify "shp"
shp_fort <- fortify.SpatialPolygonsDataFrame(shp,region="level3")
head(shp_fort);dim(shp_fort)
# rename the "level3" variable to "id" so that we can have common
fields
# to merge the dataframes using the "join" function
names(shp.DF)[1] <- "id"
# join the two dataframes, shp.DF and shp_fort
shp2 <- join(shp_fort,shp.DF,by="id")
head(shp2)
dim(shp2)
# Plot the study sites and save the graphic with ggsave
## GRAPHIC DOESN'T FILL ONE AREA OF WASATCH
utah_basins <- ggplot(shp2,aes(long,lat,group=group,fill=level3_nam))
+ geom_polygon(colour="blue")
utah_basins
ggsave(utah_basins,file="utah_basins.pdf")
